title: GPU OOM chain: recovery plan, KV journal audit, and fragmentation mitigation
creator: Aisha Khatri
description:
Summary:
A sequence of GPU OOMs across Hosted, Dedicated, and a single Private deployment was traced to an uncommon interaction between the KV journal replay path and the allocator's slab placement under bursty traffic. The symptom profile: repeated OOMs on warm nodes following sustained prefix-heavy requests, elevated KV tombstone counts, and slow compaction that allowed stale KV fragments to consume arena space.

Hypothesis (root cause):
1) A race in journal replay during tenant handoff left ephemeral tombstone metadata that prevented timely slot reuse.
2) Evictor heuristics failed to reclaim the prefix cache fast enough when a multi-tenant burst hit the same slab class, triggering allocator fragmentation and subsequent OOM cascades.
3) On Dedicated nodes the problem amplified because reserved pools kept warmed contexts alive longer; on Private a different allocator variant exacerbated the leak.

What we will deliver (scope):
- A runtime patch that introduces a journal checkpoint/acknowledgement to ensure idempotent replay and to prune ephemeral tombstones during replay.
- Incremental compaction trigger that runs synchronously after high tombstone churn events.
- Evictor policy change: ephemeral-batch eviction that prefers reclaiming high-fragation slab classes and isolates tenant-induced pressure (tenant backstop).
- A temporary conservative allocator fallback (low-latency, higher-overhead) that prevents immediate OOM while patch rolls out.
- Observability: new metrics + alert rules to detect tombstone churn, compaction latency, slab-saturation ratio, and per-tenant eviction pressure.

Workarounds provided to customers while patch lands:
- Short-term: reduce session TTLs for heavy prefix workloads, enable per-tenant burst caps, or route traffic to smaller model variants to reduce KV working set.
- For Dedicated: scheduled node rotates with drain and prewarm to avoid replay on hot nodes.
- For Private customers: a provided hotfix bundle with allocation guard toggles and a safe-config script; engineering will coordinate with SEs for on-prem application.

Trade-offs and decisions considered:
- Aggressive global compaction would add CPU overhead and transient latency; we prefer targeted incremental compaction keyed on tombstone hotspots.
- Evictor changes risk slightly higher cold-start latency for some tenants; mitigated by prewarm heuristics and the conservative allocator fallback.
- Making journal replay strictly synchronous reduces race windows but increases handoff latency; we will gate via a rollout flag and monitor tail-latency.

Acceptance criteria / exit conditions:
- Canary rollout sees zero fatal OOMs for 72h under a replay of the customer workload (simulated).
- Tombstone count for affected slab classes reduced by >= 90% after compaction pass in canary.
- No regression in median token latency >3% in hosted canary.
- Console metrics and alerts firing for "kvcache.tombstone_churn" and "allocator.slab_saturation" validated and documented.

Rollout plan:
1) Unit + integration tests merged to branch (PR linked in comments).
2) Internal canary: single-hosted rack (non-production) -> run 48h adversarial replay.
3) Production Hosted canary: <5% traffic route to patched nodes with automatic rollback if OOMs reappear or tail latency regresses beyond threshold.
4) Dedicated: staged upgrade of reserved pools with SE coordination; provide a manual backout.
5) Private: ship hotfix bundle and assist customer upgrade; patch included in runtime-1.20.

Monitoring and post-deploy tasks:
- Add Grafana panels and a console alert playbook for on-call runbooks.
- Schedule a chaos test that simulates rapid tenant handoffs + journaling replay.
- Postmortem and retro doc to be published to Confluence; customer comms draft for impacted accounts.

Links to artifacts:
- Incident doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/incidents/INC-2026-03-kv-oom-chain
- Initial repro harness (internal): https://git.redwood.ai/runtime/repro/kv-oom-harness
- PR (WIP): https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1287

Notes: this ticket combines both immediate customer remediation tasks and a longer-term runtime robustness improvement. Team should prioritize P0 production safety hooks first, then performance refactors after the canary window.

2026-03-15 - QA: Integration tests for journal checkpointing added; failing on one race (replay + compaction overlap). Investigating locking order to avoid compaction stall.
